flashcards.a: Kaynakları sentezleyip literatürdeki boşluğu (gap) göstermek ve kendi katkını oraya konumlandırmak. Özet listesi değildir.
demonstrates = kanıtlanmış kabul ediyorsun; argues = bu bir görüş, tartışmaya açık; claims = hafif şüphe bildiriyorsun.
literatür boşluğu - No published study reports 95th-percentile latency under concurrent load. The present paper addresses this gap.
verbatim copying, mosaic/patchwork, unattributed paraphrase, self-plagiarism. Kasıt gerekmez; atıf vermemek yeter.
Kelimeleri değiştirip cümle yapısını ve sırasını aynı bırakmak, üstüne atıf da vermemek. Doğru paraphrase yapıyı da değiştirir.
ve diğerleri (et alii) - Arslan et al. (2024) suggest that... Yazım: 'al' sonrası nokta, 'et' sonrası nokta yok.
ön baskı / akran değerlendirmesi - a preprint that has not yet been peer-reviewed. Güvenilirlik düzeyi belirtilmelidir.

flashcards.q: to the best of our knowledge
flashcards.a: bildiğimiz kadarıyla - özgünlük iddiasını hedge eden standart akademik kalıp.
bulgular çelişkili - Findings are mixed: while Yılmaz reports a gain, Kaya finds the opposite.
yinelemek - We make the harness public so that the results can be replicated. (Yinelenebilirlik akademik güvenin temelidir.)

questions.q: In the sample introduction, what is the stated gap in the literature?
choices: No published study reports 95th-percentile latency across a concurrency sweep with a controlled eviction policy.
Eviction policies have not been implemented in any cache.
Caching has never been applied to catalogue workloads.
Nobody has measured the average benefit of caching.
questions.explain: Boşluk cümlesi açıkça verilmiştir: *To the best of our knowledge, no published study reports 95th-percentile latency across a concurrency sweep with a controlled eviction policy.* Ortalama faydanın iyi belgelendiği ise metnin ilk paragrafında söylenir — boşluk ortalamada değil, kuyruk gecikmesindedir.

questions.q: The text says 'Kaya (2022) ... **argues** that the benefit degrades'. What does this verb choice signal?
choices: The author fully accepts Kaya's result as proven.
The author presents it as a defensible position rather than an established fact.
The author doubts Kaya's honesty.
Kaya did not publish any data.
questions.explain: **argues** bir görüşü, tartışılabilir bir konumu aktarır. Kanıtlanmış kabul edilseydi *demonstrates* ya da *shows* kullanılırdı; şüphe bildirilecek olsaydı *claims* seçilirdi. Atıf fiili yazarın duruşunu sessizce ilan eder.

questions.q: Which version avoids plagiarism?
choices: Virtual memory lets a computer make up for a lack of real memory by temporarily moving pages from RAM to disk.
Virtual memory allows a computer to compensate for a shortage of physical memory by temporarily transferring pages of data from RAM to disk storage.
When physical memory is exhausted, the operating system moves inactive pages to disk and reloads them on demand; this mechanism is known as virtual memory (Glendinning & McEwan, 2006).
As everybody knows, virtual memory compensates for a shortage of physical memory.
questions.explain: B hem yapıyı ve bakış açısını değiştirir hem atıf verir. A mosaic plagiarism (kelimeler değişmiş, yapı aynı, atıf yok), C birebir kopya, D ise kaynağı 'herkes bilir' diyerek gizler. Unutma: doğru özetleme bile atıfsızsa intihaldir.

questions.q: Even if you rewrite a source's idea entirely in your own words, you still have to cite it.
questions.explain: Doğru. Kelimeler senin olsa da **fikir** kaynağa aittir; atıf verilmeyen başka sözcüklerle anlatım (**unattributed paraphrase**) intihalin en sık görülen biçimidir. Öğrencinin yaygın yanılgısı 'kendi cümlelerimle yazdım, alıntı değil' diye düşünmektir: alıntı işareti cümleyi, atıf ise fikri korur.

questions.q: Which Latin abbreviation replaces the names of the third and further authors in an in-text citation? (write it with correct punctuation)
accept: et al.
questions.explain: **et al.** (et alii = ve diğerleri). Doğru yazım: *Arslan et al. (2024)*. 'et. al' ve 'et all' yanlıştır; nokta yalnızca kısaltılan 'al'dan sonra gelir.

questions.q: Choose the neutral reporting verb for simply relaying a measured result without taking a position: 'Demir (2021) ___ a reduction of 47%.'
accept: reports
states
notes
found
observes
questions.explain: Yansız aktarım için **reports / states / notes / observes** uygundur. *demonstrates* sonucu kanıtlanmış sayar, *claims* şüphe bildirir, *argues* görüş olarak sunar. Ölçüm sonucu aktarıyorsan en güvenli fiil **reports**tır.

questions.q: Rewrite as a synthesis sentence: 'Yılmaz (2019) studied caching. Demir (2021) studied caching too.' Use 'Both studies'.
accept: both studies examine caching
both studies investigate caching
both studies report that caching reduces latency
both studies examine the effect of caching
questions.explain: Sentez, iki kaynağı **tek cümlede ortak bir bulgu ya da ortak bir sınırlama** altında birleştirmektir: *Both studies examine caching, but neither measures concurrent access (Yılmaz, 2019; Demir, 2021).* Liste yapısı bu bağı kurmadığı için literatür taraması sayılmaz.

questions.q: Translate into academic English: 'Bildiğimiz kadarıyla bu konuyu inceleyen yayımlanmış bir çalışma yoktur.'
accept: to the best of our knowledge no published study has examined this topic
to the best of our knowledge there is no published study that has examined this topic
to the best of our knowledge no published study examines this topic
to the best of our knowledge there is no published study examining this topic
questions.explain: Standart kalıp **To the best of our knowledge, no published study has examined...**. Bu bir hedge'dir: mutlak bir yokluk iddiasını yumuşatır, çünkü hiçbir yazar tüm literatürü taradığını garanti edemez.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly signals that a source is less reliable?
choices: Arslan et al. (2024) demonstrate that eviction policy dominates tail behaviour.
According to Arslan et al. (2024), it is certain that eviction policy dominates tail behaviour.
Arslan et al. (2024) proved the dominance of eviction policy.
Arslan et al. (2024) suggest that eviction policy dominates tail behaviour, although the result has not yet been peer-reviewed.
questions.explain: B iki araç kullanır: temkinli atıf fiili (**suggest**) ve kaynağın durumuna ilişkin açık bir şerh (*has not yet been peer-reviewed*). A, C ve D ön baskıdaki bir sonucu kanıtlanmış gibi sunar — akademik dürüstlük ihlalidir.

questions.q: Write a literature review paragraph of 5-6 sentences (with invented but plausible citations) about automated code review tools. Include: a synthesis of two sources that agree, one source with a different finding, a stated gap, and your contribution sentence.
rubric: İki kaynağı ortak bir bulgu altında birleştirmeli (Both studies / Several studies report that...)
Farklı bulgu veren kaynağı karşıtlık bağlacıyla vermeli (whereas / however / by contrast)
En az üç farklı atıf fiili kullanmalı ve duruşları tutarlı olmalı
Boşluğu açıkça yazmalı (remains open / has not been examined)
'The present study addresses this gap by...' benzeri bir konumlandırma cümlesi içermeli
questions.explain: Örnek tam cevap: **Several studies report that static analysis tools detect a substantial share of defects before review: Aydın (2020) finds that 38% of null-dereference bugs are caught automatically, and Şahin (2022) reports a comparable figure for resource leaks. Both studies, however, count only defects that the tool reports, and neither measures how many true defects the tool misses. By contrast, Okan et al. (2023) argue that the main benefit of such tools is not detection but the time reviewers save on style comments, which they estimate at 22 minutes per review. Findings on developer trust are mixed: Demir (2021) notes that warnings are frequently suppressed, whereas Okan et al. observe no such behaviour in teams with a shared configuration. The effect of false-positive rate on suppression therefore remains open. The present study addresses this gap by correlating suppression events with measured false-positive rates across 40 repositories.**

questions.q: Paraphrase the following sentence correctly and add a citation: 'A mutex guarantees mutual exclusion, so only one thread can hold the lock at any given moment (Tanenbaum, 2015).' Then explain in one sentence why your version is not mosaic plagiarism.
rubric: Cümle yapısını değiştirmeli, yalnızca eşanlamlı kelime koymamalı
Teknik anlamı korumalı (tek iş parçacığı, karşılıklı dışlama)
Atıf vermeli
Mosaic plagiarism tanımına göre kendi metnini gerekçelendirmeli
Gereksiz doğrudan alıntı kullanmamalı
questions.explain: Örnek tam cevap: **If a thread has acquired a mutex, every other thread that requests it is blocked until the lock is released; this property is called mutual exclusion (Tanenbaum, 2015).** Gerekçe: *The sentence was rebuilt from a different starting point — the waiting threads rather than the mutex — and the grammatical structure, clause order and emphasis all differ from the original, while the source is still acknowledged.* Yalnızca *guarantees* yerine *ensures* yazmak mozaik intihal olurdu.

topics.title: Code Review English: Constructive Feedback, Suggestion Patterns, Handling Disagreement
topics.summary: Kod incelemesinin dili: kişiyi değil kodu eleştirme, nit/suggestion/blocking ön ekleri, nezaket derecelendirmesi, yazar tarafının yanıt kalıpları ve issue/PR başlığı yazımı.
topics.notes:
## 1. Code Review Bir İletişim Becerisidir

Kod incelemesinde iki rol vardır: **author** (değişikliği yazan) ve **reviewer** (inceleyen). Amaç kodu iyileştirmektir, kazanmak değil. Yorumun dili, teknik içeriği kadar önemlidir: aynı teknik doğru, iki farklı cümleyle yazıldığında biri işbirliği, diğeri çatışma üretir.

| BAD (kişiyi hedef alır) | GOOD (kodu ve gerekçeyi hedef alır) |
|---|---|
| You wrote this wrong. | This will throw if `items` is empty — shall we guard against that? |
| Why didn't you use a map? | A map would make this lookup O(1) instead of O(n). Worth changing? |
| This is unreadable. | I had trouble following this loop. Could we extract the filtering into a helper? |
| Terrible naming. | `d` is hard to follow. Would `deadline` be clearer? |
| I already told you this. | As we discussed in the previous PR, this path also needs the null check. |

Üç altın kural: (1) **kodu eleştir, kişiyi değil** — "you" yerine "this code" ya da "we"; (2) **gerekçe ver** — her istek bir nedenle gelir; (3) **soru sor** — emir yerine soru, yazarın bilmediğin bir gerekçesi olabileceğini kabul eder.

## 2. Yorum Ağırlığını Etiketleyin

Olgunlaşmış ekipler yorumun **bağlayıcı olup olmadığını** ön ekle bildirir. Böylece yazar nelerin zorunlu, nelerin zevk meselesi olduğunu bilir.

| Ön ek | Anlamı | Örnek |
|---|---|---|
| **nit:** | önemsiz, zorunlu değil (nitpick) | *nit: extra blank line here.* |
| **suggestion:** | öneri, yazar karar verir | *suggestion: this could be a list comprehension.* |
| **question:** | gerçek bir soru, eleştiri değil | *question: is `retries` ever negative?* |
| **issue:** / **blocking:** | düzeltilmeli, birleştirmeyi engeller | *blocking: this leaks the file handle on the error path.* |
| **praise:** | olumlu geri bildirim | *praise: nice use of a named constant here.* |
| **thought:** / **FYI:** | bilgi, eylem gerektirmez | *FYI: we are removing this module next quarter.* |
| **non-blocking:** | sonra ele alınabilir | *non-blocking: a follow-up ticket would be fine.* |

> [!ipucu]
> **nit** = *nitpick*, saç teli ayırmak, kılı kırk yarmak. "nit:" ön eki yazarın o yorumu gerekirse reddedebileceğini söyler ve gereksiz gerginliği önler. **bikeshedding** ise önemsiz ayrıntıda (boya rengi) saatlerce tartışmaktır — incelemede kaçınılması gereken davranış.

## 3. Öneri Kalıpları (Politeness Gradient)

Yumuşaktan kesine doğru:

1. *Just a thought, but ...* / *Feel free to ignore this, but ...* (en yumuşak)
2. *Have you considered ...?* / *What do you think about ...?*
3. *Could we ... ?* / *Would it make sense to ... ?*
4. *I would suggest extracting this into a helper.*
5. *Consider extracting this into a helper.* (kısa, standart, kaba değil)
6. *This needs a null check before the dereference.* (zorunlu)
7. *Blocking: this must not be merged until the token is removed from the log.* (en kesin)

Sık kullanılan hazır yorumlar:
- *Consider extracting this into a helper function.*
- *Could we rename `tmp` to something more descriptive?*
- *This looks like it duplicates `utils/format.js` — can we reuse that?*
- *What happens if the list is empty?* (edge case sorusu)
- *Is this magic number documented anywhere? Perhaps a named constant would help.*
- *Could you add a test that covers the timeout path?*
- *This is out of scope for this PR; shall we open a follow-up ticket?*
- *LGTM once the logging line is removed.* (LGTM = looks good to me)

## 4. Yazar Tarafı: Yanıt Verme ve Anlaşmazlık

| Fonksiyon | Kalıp |
|---|---|
| Kabul ve uygulama | *Good catch, fixed in 4f9a2c1.* / *Done.* / *Addressed, thanks.* |
| Kabul, sonraya bırakma | *Agreed, but I would rather do this in a follow-up — opened KRK-812.* |
| Gerekçe sunarak karşı çıkma | *I kept the loop because the list is always smaller than 10 items; a map would add allocation without a measurable gain.* |
| Bilgi isteme | *Could you clarify which path you mean? I may be missing something.* |
| Kapsam savunması | *That is a fair point, but it is outside the scope of this change.* |
| Uzlaşma | *How about a compromise: I will add the guard now and the refactor in a follow-up?* |
| Üçüncü görüşe başvurma | *We seem to disagree on this; shall we ask Ayşe for a second opinion?* |

> [!dikkat]
> "Good catch" ve "Nice catch" samimi ve yaygın kabul ifadeleridir — "You are right, I am so stupid" gibi kendini küçülten yanıtlar İngilizce profesyonel kültürde rahatsızlık yaratır. Hata kabul etmek normaldir: *Good catch, fixed.* yeterlidir.

## 5. REAL TEXT — Review Thread

```text
Pull request #412 - "Add CSV export to the reports page"
Files changed: 6   +214 -37

REVIEWER (Ayse) on reports/export.py line 44:
  blocking: the access token is written to the log on line 48. Please remove it
  or mask it; tokens must never appear in logs.

AUTHOR (Mert):
  Good catch - removed in 7c1b0ef. I also added a test that asserts the log
  line contains no "token" key.

REVIEWER (Ayse) on reports/export.py line 61:
  question: what happens if `rows` is empty? As far as I can see we would write
  a file with only a header, which may confuse users.

AUTHOR (Mert):
  That is intentional: the UI already shows "no data" before the download
  starts. I have added a comment in the code so the behaviour is not lost.

REVIEWER (Ayse) on reports/export.py line 77:
  suggestion: this nested loop is doing two things - filtering and formatting.
  Consider extracting the filtering into a helper; it would also make the unit
  test simpler. Non-blocking.

AUTHOR (Mert):
  Agreed, but I would rather keep this PR focused. Opened KRK-812 for the
  refactor and linked it in the code with a TODO.

REVIEWER (Ayse) on reports/export.py line 95:
  nit: trailing whitespace.

REVIEWER (Ayse) on tests/test_export.py line 12:
  praise: thanks for the table-driven test, this is much easier to extend.

REVIEWER (Ayse) - overall:
  Two small things left and I am happy to approve. One broader thought, purely
  FYI: we will probably move this module behind the reporting service next
  quarter, so try not to add new dependencies here.

  Status: Changes requested -> after 7c1b0ef: Approved. LGTM.
```

## 6. Nasıl Soru Açılır? (Issue / PR Başlığı Yazma)

**Issue başlığı kuralları:** emir kipi ya da kısa olgu cümlesi; 50-72 karakter; soruna odaklı, çözüme değil; bileşen ön eki faydalıdır.

| BAD | GOOD |
|---|---|
| bug | Export endpoint returns 500 when the report has no rows |
| It doesn't work!!! | CSV download fails in Safari 17 with "network error" |
| please fix asap | Login page: session expires after 30 seconds instead of 30 minutes |
| refactor stuff | reports: extract filtering logic from `export_rows()` |

**PR açıklaması şablonu:**

```text
## What
One or two sentences: what this change does.

## Why
The problem or ticket this addresses. Link: KRK-778.

## How
The approach, and any decision a reviewer should know about.

## Testing
What you ran, and what a reviewer should check manually.

## Risks / Rollback
What could go wrong and how to revert.
```

## 7. VOCABULARY

| English | Türkçe | Short definition |
|---|---|---|
| pull request (PR) | birleştirme isteği | a proposal to merge a set of changes |
| reviewer / author | inceleyen / yazan | the person who reviews and the one who wrote the change |
| to approve | onaylamak | to agree that a change can be merged |
| to request changes | değişiklik istemek | to block a merge until issues are fixed |
| nit (nitpick) | kıl payı ayrıntı | a very minor, optional comment |
| blocking / non-blocking | engelleyici / engellemeyen | must be fixed now / can wait |
| blocker | tıkayıcı sorun | something that stops work from continuing |
| to address (a comment) | (yorumu) karşılamak, gereğini yapmak | to act on feedback |
| good catch | iyi yakaladın | an informal way to accept a correction |
| LGTM (looks good to me) | bence uygun | short approval phrase |
| to extract (into a helper) | (yardımcı işleve) ayırmak | to move code into a separate function |
| to refactor | yeniden düzenlemek | to improve structure without changing behaviour |
| edge case | sınır durumu | an unusual input at the limit of valid values |
| off-by-one error | bir kayma hatası | a loop or index that is wrong by exactly one |
| magic number | sihirli sayı | an unexplained literal value in code |
| to duplicate | yinelemek, kopyalamak | to repeat the same code in two places |
| boilerplate | kalıp kod | repetitive code required by the framework |
| naming convention | adlandırma kuralı | the agreed rules for choosing names |
| maintainability | bakım kolaylığı | how easy code is to change later |
| technical debt | teknik borç | accepted shortcuts that cost time later |
| to guard against | -e karşı önlem almak | to add a check that prevents a failure |
| to push back | itiraz etmek, geri itmek | to disagree and defend your position |
| to defer | sonraya bırakmak | to postpone to a later change |
| follow-up (ticket) | takip kaydı | a separate task opened for later work |
| bikeshedding | önemsiz ayrıntıda boğulma | arguing at length about trivial details |
keyPoints: Üç kural: kodu eleştir kişiyi değil, her istek için gerekçe ver, emir yerine soru kullan.
Yorum ön ekleri ağırlığı bildirir: nit (önemsiz), suggestion, question, issue/blocking, praise, FYI, non-blocking.
Nezaket derecesi: 'Have you considered...?' < 'Could we...?' < 'Consider extracting...' < 'This needs...' < 'Blocking: ...'
'Consider extracting this into a helper' standart, kaba olmayan bir profesyonel öneri kalıbıdır.
Yazar tarafı kalıpları: Good catch, fixed in <commit>; Agreed but I would rather do this in a follow-up; That is outside the scope of this change.
Anlaşmazlıkta gerekçe ve ölçüm sunulur; çözülmezse üçüncü bir göz istenir.
Issue başlığı 50-72 karakter, soruna odaklı ve bileşen ön ekli olur: 'reports: export returns 500 for empty result'.
PR açıklaması What / Why / How / Testing / Risks bölümlerinden oluşur.
pitfalls: 'You wrote this wrong' gibi kişiyi hedef alan ikinci tekil kullanmak; 'this code' ya da 'we' tercih edilir.
Her yorumu aynı ağırlıkta yazmak: önemsiz biçim yorumuna 'nit:' koymayıp yazarı gereksiz gerginliğe sokmak.
Kendini küçülten yanıtlar ('I am so stupid, sorry'); profesyonel karşılık 'Good catch, fixed.' kadardır.
Gerekçesiz istek: 'Use a map here.' — neden, ölçüsü ne, hangi kazanç?
Kapsam dışı istekleri aynı PR'a yığmak; doğrusu follow-up ticket açıp bağlantı vermektir.
Issue başlığını 'bug', 'it doesn't work' gibi yazmak: arama ve önceliklendirme imkânsız hâle gelir.

flashcards.a: kıl payı ayrıntı, zorunlu olmayan yorum - 'nit: trailing whitespace.' Yazar gerekirse reddedebilir.
engelleyici / engellemeyen yorum - blocking: bu düzeltilmeden birleştirilemez; non-blocking: sonra ele alınabilir.
looks good to me - bence uygun, onay ifadesi. 'LGTM once the logging line is removed.'
İyi yakaladın - bir hatayı kabul etmenin standart, profesyonel ve kısa yolu: 'Good catch, fixed in 7c1b0ef.'
yardımcı işleve ayırmak - Consider extracting the filtering into a helper. (En sık kullanılan inceleme önerisi.)
sınır durumu - What happens if the list is empty? Boş liste, sıfır, negatif değer gibi uç girdiler.
sihirli sayı - koda gömülü, açıklanmamış sabit. 'Is this magic number documented? A named constant would help.'
gerekçeyle itiraz etmek - It is fine to push back on a review comment if you explain why.
takip kaydı - Agreed, but I would rather handle it in a follow-up: opened KRK-812.
önemsiz ayrıntıda uzun uzun tartışmak. İncelemede kaçınılır; bu tür yorumlara 'nit:' ön eki konur.
teknik borç - bilinçli alınan kısa yolların sonradan ödenen maliyeti.

questions.q: In the review thread, which comment is BLOCKING?
choices: the access token is written to the log and must be removed or masked
the table-driven test is easy to extend
the nested loop could be split into a helper
trailing whitespace on line 95
questions.explain: Güvenlik sorunları tipik olarak engelleyicidir ve yorumun başında **blocking:** etiketiyle verilir. Boşluk karakteri **nit:**, yardımcı işleve ayırma **suggestion: ... Non-blocking**, test övgüsü ise **praise:**tir.

questions.q: Which rewrite of 'This is unreadable.' is professionally appropriate?
choices: This code is terrible, please rewrite it.
I had trouble following this loop. Could we extract the filtering into a helper?
Why did you write it like this?
Unreadable. Fix.
questions.explain: B üç şeyi birden yapar: yargıyı **kendi deneyimine** çevirir (*I had trouble following*), somut bir eylem önerir ve soru biçiminde sorar. Diğerleri yazarı hedef alır ve uygulanabilir bir istek içermez.

questions.q: An author disagrees with a suggestion to replace a loop with a map. Which reply is the most professional?
choices: No, the loop is fine.
That is a matter of taste, moving on.
I kept the loop because the list never exceeds 10 items; a map would add an allocation without a measurable gain. Happy to change it if you think otherwise.
Everyone uses loops here.
questions.explain: B gerekçe (liste boyutu), ölçü (ölçülebilir kazanç yok) ve kapıyı açık bırakan bir kapanış içerir. Bu, **to push back** eyleminin doğru biçimidir: itiraz kişisel değil teknik ve açık uçludur.

questions.q: The prefix 'nit:' tells the author that the comment is minor and optional.
questions.explain: Doğru. **nit** (nitpick) önemsiz, zorunlu olmayan yorumu işaretler. Böylece yazar neyin birleştirmeyi engellediğini (**blocking**) neyin engellemediğini ayırt eder ve gereksiz gerginlik oluşmaz.

questions.q: In the thread, the author refuses the refactoring suggestion outright and does nothing about it.
questions.explain: Yanlış. Yazar öneriyi kabul ediyor ama PR'ı odakta tutmak için **erteliyor**: *Agreed, but I would rather keep this PR focused. Opened KRK-812... and linked it in the code with a TODO.* Bu, kapsamı korurken geri bildirimi kaybetmeyen standart çözümdür.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation LGTM stand for?
accept: looks good to me
it looks good to me
questions.explain: **LGTM = looks good to me**, yani 'bence uygun'. Koşullu kullanımı çok yaygındır: *LGTM once the logging line is removed.* Benzer kısaltmalar: **PTAL** (please take another look), **WIP** (work in progress), **IMO** (in my opinion).

questions.q: Complete the standard review suggestion: '___ extracting this into a helper function.' (one verb, imperative)
accept: consider
questions.explain: **Consider extracting this into a helper function.** Bu kalıp emir kipinde olmasına rağmen kaba değildir; 'düşün, karar senin' anlamı taşır. Daha yumuşağı *Have you considered...?*, daha kesini *This should be extracted...*

questions.q: Rewrite this aggressive comment constructively, as a question about an edge case: 'You obviously forgot empty lists again.'
accept: what happens if the list is empty
question what happens if the list is empty
what happens if rows is empty
could we handle the case where the list is empty
questions.explain: Doğru biçim kişiyi değil davranışı sorgular: **question: what happens if the list is empty?** Böylece yazarın bilinçli bir gerekçesi varsa açıklama fırsatı bulur — incelemedeki en sık yanlış varsayım, yazarın bir şeyi 'unuttuğunu' sanmaktır.

questions.q: Translate into review English: 'Bu değişikliğin kapsamı dışında; bir takip kaydı açalım mı?'
accept: this is out of scope for this change shall we open a follow up ticket
this is outside the scope of this change shall we open a follow up ticket
this is out of scope for this pr shall we open a follow up ticket
that is out of scope for this change shall we open a follow up ticket
questions.explain: İki kalıp birlikte: **out of scope for this change / PR** ve **shall we open a follow-up ticket?** Kapsamı korumanın nazik yolu, isteği reddetmek değil başka bir yere taşımaktır.

questions.q: Which issue title follows the conventions given in the notes?
choices: Bug in export
IT DOESN'T WORK PLEASE FIX ASAP
Maybe we should think about refactoring the export code someday
reports: export endpoint returns 500 when the result set is empty
questions.explain: C bileşen ön eki (**reports:**), gözlenen davranış (500 döner) ve koşulu (boş sonuç kümesi) içeriyor; 72 karakterin altında ve aranabilir. A fazla genel, B duygusal ve bilgisiz, D ise bir başlık değil belirsiz bir dilek.

questions.q: Write five review comments in English for an imaginary pull request. Use a different prefix for each: nit, question, suggestion, blocking, praise. Each comment must give a reason.
rubric: Beş farklı ön eki doğru kullanmalı
Her yorumda gerekçe ya da etki bilgisi olmalı
Kişiyi hedef alan ikinci tekil suçlama içermemeli
blocking yorumu gerçekten engelleyici bir konuda olmalı (güvenlik, veri kaybı, sızıntı)
En az bir yorum soru biçiminde olmalı
questions.explain: Örnek tam cevap: **nit: two blank lines between the imports and the class — our style guide asks for one. question: is `timeout_ms` ever zero? If it is, the retry loop would spin without waiting. suggestion: this 30-line function does parsing and validation; extracting the validation would make both parts testable. Non-blocking. blocking: the password is included in the exception message on line 82, so it would end up in the error tracker; please redact it. praise: the named constants at the top of the file make the magic numbers from the old version unnecessary — nice improvement.**

questions.q: Write a PR description in English for a change that adds pagination to an API endpoint. Use the What / Why / How / Testing / Risks template.
rubric: Beş bölümün hepsi bulunmalı
What bölümü bir iki cümlede ne yapıldığını söylemeli
Why bölümü sorunu ve varsa kaydı (ticket) bağlamalı
Testing bölümü inceleyenin elle ne kontrol edeceğini söylemeli
Risks bölümünde geri alma yolu belirtilmeli
Cümleler kısa ve etken çatıda olmalı
questions.explain: Örnek tam cevap: **## What** — *Adds cursor-based pagination to `GET /api/v1/courses` with `limit` (default 25, max 100) and `cursor` parameters.* **## Why** — *The endpoint currently returns all 3,400 rows, which makes the course list page take 3.4 s to load (KRK-778).* **## How** — *The query now orders by `(created_at, id)` and returns an opaque cursor. The old unpaginated behaviour is preserved when no parameters are given, so existing clients keep working.* **## Testing** — *Added unit tests for the cursor encoder and an integration test for the last page. Manually checked the course list page in Chrome and Safari; please verify the mobile client, which I could not build locally.* **## Risks / Rollback** — *A malformed cursor now returns 400 instead of 200. The change is behind the `pagination` feature flag and can be disabled without a deployment.*

topics.title: Agile Team Communication: Standups, Sprint Planning, Retrospectives, Writing Issues
topics.summary: Günlük standup'ın üç cümlesi, kestirim ve kapasite dili, kişiyi değil süreci ele alan retrospektif ifadeleri ve yeniden üretilebilir bir iş kaydı (issue) gövdesi yazma.
topics.notes:
## 1. Çevik Takımın Dört Konuşma Ortamı

Çevik (agile) ekipte İngilizce, uzun raporlardan çok **kısa ve sık** iletişimle kullanılır. Dört ortamın dili birbirinden farklıdır:

| Ortam | Süre | Amaç | Dil |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Daily standup** | 10-15 dk | durum + engel | çok kısa, geçmiş-şimdi-engel |
| **Sprint planning** | 1-2 saat | ne alınacak, ne kadar iş | kestirim, kapasite, taahhüt |
| **Sprint review / demo** | 30-60 dk | sonucu göstermek | sunum, paydaş dili |
| **Retrospective** | 45-60 dk | süreci iyileştirmek | dürüst, kişisel olmayan, eylem odaklı |

## 2. Daily Standup: Üç Cümle Yeter

Klasik kalıp: **yesterday -> today -> impediments**. Rapor değil, senkronizasyondur: ayrıntı tartışması standup'tan sonraya bırakılır (*let us take that offline*).

**BAD (uzun, teknik derinliğe dalıyor, engel belirsiz):**
> So yesterday I was working on the export thing, I looked at the code and it was quite complicated because there is this old function, and I tried a few approaches, and then I realized that maybe the serializer... anyway it is still not working, I will continue.

**GOOD (20 saniye, net, engel adlandırılmış):**
> Yesterday I finished the CSV encoder and opened PR 412. Today I am adding the empty-result test and reviewing Ayşe's migration. One impediment: I still need read access to the staging database — Can someone grant that after the call?

Yararlı kalıplar:
- *Yesterday I finished / wrapped up / pushed / reviewed...*
- *Today I am picking up KRK-812. / I am continuing with the migration.*
- *No blockers.* / *I am blocked on KRK-801 until the API key arrives.*
- *I am waiting on the design review.* (başka birine bağlı olmak)
- *Quick heads-up: the staging environment will be down at 14:00.*
- *Let us take that offline.* / *Let us pick this up after the standup.*
- *Could you loop me in on that thread?* (beni de dahil et)
- *I will circle back on this by the end of the day.* (geri döneceğim)

## 3. Sprint Planning: Kestirim ve Taahhüt Dili

| İşlev | Kalıplar |
|---|---|
| İş tanımı | *As a student, I want to filter courses by semester, so that I can find my own courses quickly.* (user story) |
| Kabul ölçütü | *Acceptance criteria: the filter persists after a page reload; an empty result shows a message.* |
| Kestirim | *I would estimate this at three points.* / *This feels like a two-day task.* / *That is a rough estimate.* |
| Belirsizlik | *There are too many unknowns; shall we run a spike first?* |
| Kapasite | *We have two people on call this sprint, so our capacity is lower than usual.* |
| Bölme | *This story is too big — can we split it into the API part and the UI part?* |
| Taahhüt | *We are committing to items 1 to 5; item 6 is a stretch goal.* |
| Bitti tanımı | *Our definition of done includes tests, documentation and a deployed preview.* |

> [!ipucu]
> **estimate** (kestirim) bir **taahhüt (commitment)** değildir. İngilizcede bu ayrımı korumak profesyonellik göstergesidir: *That is an estimate, not a commitment. If the data migration turns out to be dirty, it could take two days longer.*

## 4. Retrospektif: Dürüst Ama Kişisel Olmayan

Retrospektifin dili tek bir ilkeye dayanır: **kişiyi değil süreci ele al.** Klasik üç sütun: *What went well? / What did not go well? / What will we try next?*

| BAD (kişiyi suçlar, eylem yok) | GOOD (süreci tarif eder, eylem önerir) |
|---|---|
| Mert broke the build again. | The build was broken for 6 hours on Tuesday because the pipeline does not run tests on the release branch. Shall we enable that check? |
| Nobody reviews my PRs. | Review requests waited 2.4 days on average this sprint. I would suggest a daily 20-minute review slot. |
| Planning was a disaster. | We committed to 34 points and delivered 19, mainly because two stories had no acceptance criteria. |
| QA is slow. | Testing started on the last day of the sprint, which left no time to fix findings. Could we hand over features as they are finished? |

Kalıplar:
- *What went well: ... / What did not go well: ... / What we will try next: ...*
- *One thing I would do differently is ...*
- *I felt that ... , although I may be missing context.* (birinci tekil duygu ifadesi retrospektifte kabul edilir)
- *The main takeaway for me is ...* (çıkardığım ders)
- *Action item: Ayşe will add the test step to the pipeline by Friday.*
- *Kudos to Mert for picking up the on-call shift.* (teşekkür, takdir)
- *Let us timebox this discussion to five minutes.*

## 5. REAL TEXT — Retrospective Notes

```text
SPRINT 24 RETROSPECTIVE - 4 April, 55 minutes, 6 participants
Facilitator: Ayse   Notes: Mert

WHAT WENT WELL
  - The CSV export shipped two days before the end of the sprint, and the
    customer confirmed it on the same day.
  - Pair programming on the migration worked better than expected; both Mert
    and Elif can now run it unaided, so we no longer depend on one person.
  - Kudos to Elif for taking the on-call shift at short notice.

WHAT DID NOT GO WELL
  - We committed to 34 story points and completed 19. Two of the unfinished
    stories had no acceptance criteria, so "done" was unclear and both were
    reopened after review.
  - Review requests waited an average of 2.4 days. Three people reported that
    they were blocked while waiting.
  - The staging database was out of date for most of the sprint. Nobody owned
    refreshing it, so everybody assumed somebody else would.
  - The build stayed red for six hours on Tuesday. The pipeline does not run
    tests on release branches, which is how the regression reached staging.

WHAT WE WILL TRY NEXT
  1. No story enters the sprint without acceptance criteria. The team will
     reject unrefined items during planning. Owner: whole team, from sprint 25.
  2. A 20-minute review slot at 11:00 every day. Owner: Ayse to add the
     calendar entry this week.
  3. Staging refresh becomes part of the weekly rotation, with a named owner
     each week. Owner: Mert to write the runbook by 11 April.
  4. Enable the test stage on release branches. Owner: Elif, by 8 April.

DISCUSSION PARKED
  - Whether to move to two-week demos instead of one-week demos. We timeboxed
    this and will take it to the next retrospective.

TAKEAWAY
  Most of what we lost this sprint was lost while waiting - for reviews, for
  data, for a definition of done - rather than while writing code.
```

## 6. Issue / Ticket Gövdesi Yazmak

PR açıklamasını geçen hafta gördük. İş kaydı (issue) gövdesinin de bir iskeleti var:

```text
Title: reports: CSV export omits the last row when the result set is odd

Summary
  The CSV export writes one row fewer than the table shows when the number of
  rows is odd.

Steps to reproduce
  1. Open /reports with a filter that returns 7 rows.
  2. Click "Export CSV".
  3. Open the downloaded file.

Expected
  7 data rows plus the header.

Actual
  6 data rows plus the header.

Environment
  Staging, build 2025.4.2, Chrome 134, reproduced on 3 of 3 attempts.

Impact / priority
  Customers use these files for accounting, so silent data loss is serious.
  Suggested priority: P1.

Notes
  The boundary looks like an off-by-one in the chunking loop in export.py:61.
```

> [!dikkat]
> Türkçe "bende çalışmıyor" ifadesinin doğrudan çevirisi olan *"It doesn't work at me"* yanlıştır. Doğrusu: **It does not work on my machine.** / **I cannot reproduce it locally.** Ayrıca *"I am waiting your answer"* değil **I am waiting for your answer** ya da **I look forward to your reply**.

## 7. VOCABULARY

| English | Türkçe | Short definition |
|---|---|---|
| standup | ayakta toplantı, günlük senkron | a short daily meeting on status and obstacles |
| sprint / iteration | koşu, yineleme | a fixed short period of planned work |
| backlog | iş havuzu, bekleyen işler | the ordered list of work not yet started |
| to refine / to groom | (işi) olgunlaştırmak | to clarify and size backlog items before planning |
| user story | kullanıcı hikâyesi | a need described from the user's point of view |
| acceptance criteria | kabul ölçütleri | the conditions that make a story complete |
| definition of done | bitti tanımı | the team's shared standard for finished work |
| story point | iş puanı | a relative measure of effort |
| velocity | hız (tamamlanan puan) | how much a team completes per sprint |
| capacity | kapasite | how much work the team can take this sprint |
| estimate vs commitment | kestirim / taahhüt | a best guess versus a promise |
| impediment | engel, takoz | anything that stops progress |
| to unblock | engeli kaldırmak | to remove what is stopping someone |
| to be waiting on | -i bekliyor olmak | to depend on someone else's action |
| spike | araştırma işi | a short investigation to reduce uncertainty |
| to timebox | süre sınırı koymak | to limit a discussion to a fixed time |
| to pick up (a ticket) | (bir işi) üzerine almak | to start working on a task |
| to hand over | devretmek | to pass work to another person |
| work in progress (WIP) | süren iş | tasks started but not finished |
| retrospective | değerlendirme toplantısı | a meeting to improve how the team works |
| takeaway | çıkarılan ders, ana sonuç | the main lesson from a discussion |
| kudos | takdir, aferin | public recognition of good work |
| heads-up | önceden uyarı | advance notice of something |
| to loop someone in | birini (yazışmaya) katmak | to include someone in a conversation |
| to circle back | geri dönmek (konuya) | to return to a topic later |
| to take it offline | toplantı dışına taşımak | to discuss separately, not in the meeting |
keyPoints: Standup kalıbı: yesterday -> today -> impediments. Ayrıntı tartışması 'let us take that offline' ile sonraya bırakılır.
Engel belirsiz bırakılmaz: 'I am blocked on KRK-801 until the API key arrives.'
User story kalıbı: As a <role>, I want <goal>, so that <benefit>. Yanında acceptance criteria bulunur.
estimate (kestirim) taahhüt değildir; bu ayrımı açıkça söylemek profesyoneldir.
Belirsizlik çoksa kestirim yerine spike (kısa araştırma) önerilir.
Retrospektif dili kişiyi değil süreci tarif eder ve her maddeyi sahipli bir action item'a bağlar.
Retrospektif üç sütunu: what went well / what did not go well / what we will try next; ayrıca takeaway ve kudos.
Issue gövdesi: summary, steps to reproduce, expected, actual, environment, impact/priority, notes.
pitfalls: Standup'ta durum raporu yerine teknik hikâye anlatmak; engeli adlandırmadan 'hâlâ uğraşıyorum' demek.
Retrospektifte kişi adı vererek suçlamak: 'Mert broke the build again' yerine süreç eksiğini tarif et.
'It doesn't work at me' gibi doğrudan çeviri; doğrusu 'It does not work on my machine.'
'I am waiting your answer' — waiting fiili 'for' ister: 'I am waiting for your answer.'
Kestirimi taahhüt gibi sunmak ya da hiç sayı vermemek; ikisi de planlamayı bozar.
Eylemsiz retrospektif: şikâyetler listelenir ama sahip ve tarih yazılmaz.

flashcards.a: yesterday (ne bitti) -> today (ne yapılacak) -> impediments (engel var mı). 20-30 saniye yeterlidir.
engel / engeli kaldırmak - I am blocked on the API key; could someone unblock me after the call?
kabul ölçütleri - The filter persists after a page reload; an empty result shows a message. ('Bitti'yi tanımlar.)
As a student, I want to filter courses by semester, so that I can find my own courses quickly.
kestirim bir tahmindir, taahhüt bir sözdür. 'That is an estimate, not a commitment.'
belirsizliği azaltmak için yapılan kısa araştırma işi - There are too many unknowns; shall we run a spike first?
süre sınırı koymak - Let us timebox this discussion to five minutes. (Retrospektifte dağılmayı önler.)
çıkarılan ders, ana sonuç - The main takeaway is that we lost most time while waiting, not while coding.
önceden uyarı - Quick heads-up: the staging environment will be down at 14:00.

flashcards.q: to loop someone in / to circle back
flashcards.a: birini yazışmaya katmak / konuya sonra geri dönmek. 'Could you loop me in?' 'I will circle back by Friday.'
toplantı dışına taşımak - Let us take that offline. (Ayrıntıyı standup'ta tartışmamak için kullanılır.)

questions.q: According to the retrospective notes, what was the main reason two stories were reopened after review?
choices: They had no acceptance criteria, so 'done' was unclear
Review requests waited 2.4 days
The staging database was out of date
The build was red for six hours
questions.explain: Metin: *Two of the unfinished stories had no acceptance criteria, so 'done' was unclear and both were reopened after review.* Diğer üç madde de gerçek sorunlardır ama yeniden açılmanın nedeni olarak **kabul ölçütü eksikliği** gösterilmiştir.

questions.q: Which standup contribution is best?
choices: I worked on stuff yesterday and I will continue today.
Yesterday I finished the CSV encoder and opened PR 412. Today I am adding the empty-result test. One impediment: I need read access to the staging database.
Let me explain the whole serializer design, it is quite complicated...
Everything is fine, no news.
questions.explain: B üç parçayı da veriyor: dün ne bitti (somut, PR numarasıyla), bugün ne yapılacak, hangi engel var ve kimden ne isteniyor. A içeriksiz, C standup'ı sunuma çeviriyor (*take it offline*), D ise engel sorusunu yanıtlamıyor.

questions.q: Which retrospective item is written in the recommended style?
choices: QA is always slow and nobody cares.
Mert broke the build again on Tuesday.
Testing started on the last day of the sprint, which left no time to fix findings. Could we hand over features as they are finished?
Planning was a disaster this time.
questions.explain: B süreci tarif ediyor, etkisini söylüyor ve bir iyileştirme önerisi sunuyor — kişi adı geçmiyor. A ve D duygusal genelleme, C ise kişiyi hedef alıyor. Retrospektifin tek ilkesi: **kişiyi değil süreci ele al.**

questions.q: 'That is an estimate, not a commitment' is an acceptable and professional thing to say in sprint planning.
questions.explain: Doğru. Kestirim ile taahhüdü ayırmak, hem takımı hem paydaşı korur. Ardından belirsizlik kaynağı söylenir: *If the migrated data turns out to be dirty, it could take two days longer.* Bu, hedge dilinin planlamadaki karşılığıdır.

questions.q: 'I am waiting for your answer' is correct English.
questions.explain: Doğru. **wait** fiili nesnesini **for** edatıyla alır: *wait for a reply / for the build to finish*. Türkçedeki 'cevabınızı bekliyorum' yapısı edatsız olduğu için *I am waiting your answer* hatası çok sık üretilir. Daha resmî seçenek: *I look forward to your reply.*

questions.q: Which English word (used in agile meetings) means 'anything that stops your progress'?
accept: impediment
an impediment
blocker
a blocker
questions.explain: **impediment** (Scrum'ın resmî terimi) ya da gündelik kullanımda **blocker**. Fiil hâli: *I am blocked on X.* Engeli kaldırmak: **to unblock**.

questions.q: Complete the user story: 'As a student, I want to filter courses by semester, ___ I can find my own courses quickly.' (two words)
accept: so that
questions.explain: Kullanıcı hikâyesinin üçüncü parçası faydayı bildirir ve **so that** ile bağlanır: *As a <role>, I want <goal>, so that <benefit>.* Fayda yazılmadığında ekip işin niçin yapıldığını bilmez ve kabul ölçütü kurulamaz.

questions.q: Rewrite without blaming a person: 'Mert broke the build again on Tuesday.' Begin with 'The build'.
accept: the build was broken for six hours on tuesday because the pipeline does not run tests on the release branch
the build was broken on tuesday because the pipeline does not run tests on release branches
the build was broken on tuesday because the pipeline does not run tests on the release branch
questions.explain: Edilgen çatı burada tam yerindedir: eyleyen önemsizdir, önemli olan **sürecin neden izin verdiğidir**. Bu yaklaşım 'blameless postmortem' kültürünün dilidir ve aynı hatanın tekrarını engelleyecek eylemi görünür kılar.

questions.q: Translate into English: 'Bunu toplantı dışına taşıyalım ve gün sonunda konuya geri döneyim.'
accept: let us take that offline and i will circle back at the end of the day
lets take that offline and i will circle back at the end of the day
let us take this offline and i will circle back by the end of the day
let us take that offline and i will circle back by the end of the day
questions.explain: İki deyim: **to take it offline** (toplantı dışında görüşmek) ve **to circle back** (konuya sonra dönmek). 'out of the meeting' ya da 'turn back to the subject' doğal değildir.

questions.q: A story has too many unknowns to estimate. What is the standard agile proposal in English?
choices: Let us just double the estimate.
Let us timebox the sprint.
Let us mark it as a blocker.
Shall we run a spike first to reduce the unknowns?
questions.explain: **spike** belirsizliği azaltmak için yapılan, süresi sınırlı bir araştırma işidir. Kestirimi ikiye katlamak belirsizliği gizler, timebox bir tartışma tekniğidir, blocker ise engeldir — hiçbiri bilgi eksikliğini gidermez.

questions.q: Write a complete issue (ticket) in English for this bug: the login page keeps the user logged in for only 30 seconds instead of 30 minutes, on staging, Firefox, every time. Use the sections Title / Summary / Steps to reproduce / Expected / Actual / Environment / Impact.
rubric: Başlık bileşen ön ekli, kısa ve soruna odaklı olmalı
Adımlar numaralı ve yeniden üretilebilir olmalı
Expected ve Actual ayrı ayrı ve ölçülü yazılmalı
Environment bölümünde ortam, tarayıcı ve yeniden üretim oranı olmalı
Impact bölümünde kullanıcı etkisi ve önerilen öncelik olmalı
Duygusal ifade ('it doesn't work!!!') içermemeli
questions.explain: Örnek tam cevap: **Title:** *auth: session expires after 30 seconds instead of 30 minutes.* **Summary:** *On staging, an authenticated session is invalidated after roughly 30 seconds, so the user is redirected to the login page during normal use.* **Steps to reproduce:** *1. Log in at /login with a test account. 2. Wait 45 seconds without interacting. 3. Click any menu item.* **Expected:** *The session remains valid for 30 minutes of inactivity.* **Actual:** *The request returns 401 and the user is redirected to /login.* **Environment:** *Staging, build 2025.4.2, Firefox 126, reproduced on 5 of 5 attempts; not reproducible in production.* **Impact:** *Unusable for manual testing and for the customer demo on Friday; suggested priority P1. The session TTL in the staging config appears to be set in seconds rather than minutes.*

questions.q: Write a short retrospective contribution in English (4-5 sentences) about a sprint in which code reviews were slow. Include one 'what did not go well' observation with a number, one feeling statement, and one action item with an owner and a date.
rubric: Gözlemi sayıyla vermeli (ortalama bekleme süresi gibi)
Kişi suçlamamalı, süreci tarif etmeli
Duygu ifadesini uygun kalıpla vermeli (I felt that...)
Action item sahipli ve tarihli olmalı
En az bir retrospektif kalıbı kullanmalı (what did not go well / takeaway / I would do differently)
questions.explain: Örnek tam cevap: **What did not go well: review requests waited 2.4 days on average this sprint, and three of us were blocked while waiting. I felt that my changes were getting stale, although I may be missing context about how busy the reviewers were. One thing I would do differently is to split large pull requests, because the two PRs above 600 lines took the longest. Action item: Ayşe will add a daily 20-minute review slot at 11:00 to the calendar this week, and we will check the average waiting time again in the next retrospective. My main takeaway is that waiting cost us more than coding did.**

topics.title: Customer and Stakeholder Communication: Eliciting Requirements, Scope Change, Delivering Bad News
topics.summary: Müşteriye etkiyi önce yazma, açık uçlu gereksinim soruları, scope creep karşısında bedeli görünür kılma ve kötü haberi sorumluluk alarak verme.
topics.notes:
## 1. Müşteri İletişimi Neden Farklıdır?

Ekip içi yazışmada ortak bağlam vardır; müşteride yoktur. Müşteri **teknik ayrıntıyı değil etkiyi** anlamak ister: ne zaman çalışacak, bana ne maliyeti olacak, riskim ne. Üç ilke:

1. **Etkiyi önce yaz, teknik açıklamayı sonra.** (BLUF: bottom line up front)
2. **Söz verdiğin şeyin sınırını yaz.** Belirsizliği gizlemek kısa vadede rahat, uzun vadede felakettir.
3. **Jargonu çevir.** *"The N+1 query in the ORM causes a cache stampede"* yerine *"the page makes one database request per course, which is why it is slow with many courses"*.

**BAD (teknik, savunmacı, etkisi belirsiz):**
> Due to the fact that the ORM was generating an N+1 query pattern and the cache was not being invalidated, the sprint scope could not be fully completed as originally anticipated.

**GOOD (etki önce, sade, eylem var):**
> The report page will be ready on 18 June instead of 11 June. We found that it loads one record at a time, which makes it unusably slow with your full dataset, and fixing this properly takes one additional week. Everything else in the release is unaffected, and we can give you a preview with a smaller dataset on Thursday if that helps.

## 2. Gereksinim Toplama Soruları (Requirement Elicitation)

İyi sorular kapalı değil **açık** uçludur ve varsayımları sınar.

| Amaç | Soru kalıpları |
|---|---|
| Bağlam | *Could you walk me through how you do this today?* / *Who else is involved in this process?* |
| Amaç | *What problem would this solve for you?* / *What would success look like six months from now?* |
| Ölçek | *Roughly how many records are we talking about?* / *How often does this happen?* |
| Sınır | *What must never happen?* / *Are there any regulatory constraints we should know about?* |
| Öncelik | *If we could only deliver one of these, which would it be?* / *Is that a must-have or a nice-to-have?* |
| Uç durum | *What should happen if two people edit the same record?* |
| Varsayım testi | *I am assuming the data arrives daily. Is that correct?* |
| Kabul | *How will you decide whether this is working?* |

> [!ipucu]
> **Must-have / should-have / nice-to-have** ayrımı (MoSCoW) müşteriyle önceliklendirmenin en pratik dilidir. Her istek "kritik" olduğunda hiçbir şey kritik değildir: *Let us mark these three as must-have for launch and the rest as nice-to-have.*

## 3. Kapsam Değişikliği ve Scope Creep

**Scope creep**: kapsamın, kimse fark etmeden küçük eklerle büyümesi. Dili öğrenmenin amacı "hayır" demek değil, **her ekin bedelini görünür kılmaktır**.

| Durum | Kalıp |
|---|---|
| Kaydetmek | *Let me note that as a change request so that we can cost it properly.* |
| Bedelini göstermek | *We can add that. It would move the delivery date from 11 to 18 June — shall we proceed?* |
| Ödünleşim sunmak | *We can fit it into this release if we postpone the export feature. Which of the two is more valuable to you?* |
| Kapsam dışını hatırlatmak | *As agreed in the statement of work, multi-currency support is outside the current scope.* |
| Onay istemek | *Could you confirm this in writing so that I can update the plan?* |
| Sınır çizmek (nazik) | *I would rather not commit to that today; let me check with the team and come back to you tomorrow.* |

**BAD (hem kabul ediyor hem bedelini söylemiyor):** *Sure, no problem, we will add it.*
**GOOD:** *We can add it. Based on a first look it is about three days of work, which would push the release to 18 June. If the date matters more, we could ship it in the following release instead.*

## 4. Kötü Haber Verme

İngilizce profesyonel kültürde kötü haberin sırası şudur: **bağlam -> haber (açıkça) -> neden (kısa) -> eylem planı -> telafi -> özür (abartısız).**

**BAD (gömülü haber, savunmacı, belirsiz):**
> I hope this email finds you well. As you may be aware, we have been working very hard on the project and unfortunately, due to a number of unforeseen circumstances beyond our control, there may possibly be some delay in certain deliverables, but we are doing our best.

**GOOD:**
> I am writing to let you know that the reporting module will be delivered on 18 June, one week later than planned. While testing with your full dataset we found that the page loads one record at a time, which makes it too slow to use; rebuilding that query properly takes a week. To limit the impact, we will release the rest of the module on 11 June as planned, and I will send you a working preview on Thursday. I am sorry for the change at short notice — I should have tested with the full dataset earlier, and we have added that step to our checklist.

Yararlı kalıplar: *I am writing to let you know that...*, *Unfortunately, we will not be able to ... by ...*, *The reason is that ...*, *To limit the impact, we will ...*, *I want to be upfront about the risk that ...*, *I am sorry for the disruption this causes.*, *I take responsibility for ...*

> [!dikkat]
> *"I am sorry for any inconvenience this may have caused"* aşırı kullanılmış, mesafeli ve içtenlikten uzak bir kalıptır. Somut özür daha güçlüdür: **I am sorry that you had to find this out from your own customer.** Aynı şekilde "as per our conversation", "please be advised", "kindly do the needful" gibi eski kalıplardan kaçın; "as we discussed", "please note", "could you please..." kullan.

## 5. REAL TEXT — Customer E-mail

```text
Subject: Reporting module: new date 18 June (was 11 June)

Dear Ms Kaya,

I am writing to let you know that the reporting module will now be delivered on
18 June, one week later than we agreed.

While testing with a copy of your full dataset we found that the report page
sends one database request for each course, which means it needs about 40
seconds to open for your 3,400 courses. The page was fast with our test data,
so we did not see this earlier. Rewriting that part properly takes five working
days, including tests.

This is what we propose:

  - 11 June: we release everything else in the module, as planned. The export
    and the filters are unaffected.
  - 12 June: you receive a preview link of the new report page with a reduced
    dataset, so that your team can confirm the layout.
  - 18 June: the full report page goes live, with a target load time below two
    seconds for your dataset.

Nothing else in the schedule changes, and there is no additional cost for you.
The training session planned for 25 June can go ahead as arranged.

I am sorry for the late notice. We should have tested with production-sized
data before we committed to the date, and we have now added that step to our
release checklist.

If the 18 June date causes a problem on your side, could we have a short call
tomorrow to look at the options together? I am available between 10:00 and
15:00.

Kind regards,
Mert Aydın
Project Lead, KRK Software
+90 318 000 00 00
```

Neden işliyor? Konu satırı haberi **taşıyor**; ilk cümlede yeni tarih var; neden kısa ve jargonsuz; plan tarihli ve maddeli; ne değişmediği de söylenmiş (*nothing else in the schedule changes*); özür somut ve düzeltici eylemle birlikte; son paragraf kapıyı açık bırakıyor.

## 6. Selamlama ve Ton Ölçeği

| Durum | Açılış | Kapanış |
|---|---|---|
| Adını bilmiyorsun, resmî | *Dear Sir or Madam,* (yalnızca gerçekten bilinmiyorsa) | *Yours faithfully,* |
| Adını biliyorsun, resmî | *Dear Ms Kaya,* | *Kind regards,* / *Yours sincerely,* |
| İş arkadaşı, nötr | *Hello Elif,* / *Hi Elif,* | *Best regards,* / *Best,* |
| Tanıdık, gündelik | *Hi Elif,* | *Thanks,* / *Cheers,* |

Yumuşatma araçları: **Could you...?** (Can you...'dan nazik), *Would you mind...?*, *I was wondering whether...*, *It would be helpful if...*, *Just to make sure I understood correctly, ...*

## 7. VOCABULARY

| English | Türkçe | Short definition |
|---|---|---|
| to elicit (requirements) | (gereksinimi) ortaya çıkarmak | to draw information out through questions |
| constraint | kısıt | a limit that cannot be changed |
| must-have / nice-to-have | olmazsa olmaz / iyi olur | essential versus optional |
| scope creep | kapsam kayması, kapsamın şişmesi | uncontrolled growth of what was agreed |
| change request | değişiklik talebi | a formal request to alter the agreed scope |
| statement of work | iş tanımı belgesi | the contract document defining the work |
| sign-off | onay, imza | formal approval that something is accepted |
| to set expectations | beklentiyi yönetmek | to make clear what will and will not happen |
| to commit to (a date) | (bir tarihe) taahhüt vermek | to promise formally |
| to slip (a date) | (tarih) kaymak | to be delivered later than planned |
| to push back (a date) | (tarihi) ileriye almak | to postpone a deadline |
| contingency | pay, yedek süre/bütçe | extra time or money kept for surprises |
| ballpark figure | kabaca rakam | a rough approximate number |
| to escalate | üst makama taşımak | to raise an issue to a higher level |
| point of contact | muhatap, irtibat kişisi | the named person to communicate with |
| onboarding | işe/ürüne alıştırma süreci | the process of getting someone started |
| to onboard (a customer) | (müşteriyi) sisteme almak | to set up and train a new user |
| upfront | baştan, açıkça | openly and in advance |
| to reiterate | yeniden belirtmek | to say something again for clarity |
| goodwill gesture | iyi niyet jesti | something given to repair a relationship |
| to take responsibility | sorumluluğu üstlenmek | to accept that a fault is yours |
| disruption | aksama, kesinti | serious interruption of normal work |
| at short notice | son anda, kısa sürede haber verilerek | with little warning |
| to go ahead as arranged | planlandığı gibi devam etmek | to happen as previously agreed |
keyPoints: Müşteriye yazarken etki önce gelir (BLUF), teknik açıklama sonra ve jargonsuz olur.
Gereksinim soruları açık uçludur ve varsayımı sınar: 'Could you walk me through how you do this today?'
Önceliklendirme dili: must-have / should-have / nice-to-have; 'hepsi kritik' bilgi taşımaz.
Scope creep'e 'hayır' demek gerekmez; her ekin tarih ve maliyet bedeli görünür kılınır.
Kapsam değişikliği change request olarak kaydedilir ve yazılı onay istenir.
Kötü haber sırası: bağlam -> haber -> kısa neden -> plan -> telafi -> somut özür.
Konu satırı haberi taşır: 'Reporting module: new date 18 June (was 11 June)'.
'I am sorry for any inconvenience this may have caused' klişesi yerine somut özür ve düzeltici eylem yazılır.
Dear Sir or Madam yalnızca muhatabın adı gerçekten bilinmiyorsa kullanılır; adını biliyorsan 'Dear Ms Kaya'.
pitfalls: Kötü haberi paragrafın ortasına gömmek ve 'I hope this email finds you well' ile başlamak.
Belirsiz teminat vermek: 'Sure, no problem, we will add it.' — tarih ve maliyet etkisi söylenmeden kabul.
Müşteriye jargonla yazmak: N+1 query, cache stampede gibi terimleri çevirmeden kullanmak.
Aşırı resmî ve eski kalıplar: 'Please be advised', 'as per our conversation', 'kindly do the needful'.
Emir kipini insana yöneltmek: 'Send me the data today.' yerine 'Could you send me the data today?'
Sorumluluğu 'unforeseen circumstances beyond our control' diye dağıtmak; somut neden ve düzeltici eylem beklenir.

flashcards.a: kapsam kayması - kapsamın küçük eklerle kontrolsüz büyümesi. Çözüm: her eki change request olarak kaydetmek.
değişiklik talebi - Let me note that as a change request so that we can cost it properly.
olmazsa olmaz / iyi olur - Is that a must-have or a nice-to-have for launch? (Önceliklendirmenin en pratik dili.)
beklentiyi yönetmek - Setting expectations early is cheaper than apologizing later.

flashcards.q: to slip / to push back (a date)
flashcards.a: tarihin kayması / tarihi ileriye almak - The date slipped by one week. We had to push the release back to 18 June.
son anda haber verilerek - I am sorry for the change at short notice. (Özür cümlelerinde sık geçer.)
baştan, açıkça - I want to be upfront about the risk that the migration may take longer.
kabaca rakam - Could you give me a ballpark figure? (Kesin kestirim istemeden büyüklük sormak.)
üst makama taşımak - If we cannot agree, I will escalate this to the steering committee.
Could daha dolaylı ve naziktir. Emir kipi ('Send me the data') insana yönelikken sert duyulur; kılavuzda ise doğrudur.

flashcards.q: Dear Sir or Madam ne zaman kullanılır?
flashcards.a: Yalnızca muhatabın adı gerçekten bilinmiyorsa. Adını biliyorsan 'Dear Ms Kaya,' yaz; kapanış 'Kind regards' olur.

questions.q: Why does the customer e-mail state the new date in the subject line and the first sentence?
choices: So that the reader learns the most important fact immediately (bottom line up front)
To avoid having to give a reason
Because English e-mails must always repeat the subject
To make the e-mail look longer
questions.explain: Kötü haberi gizlemek güveni bozar. **BLUF (bottom line up front)** ilkesi gereği sonuç önce gelir; gerekçe sonra ve kısa verilir. Mektup yine de neden, plan ve özür bölümlerini içerir — haber öne alınınca bunlar atlanmaz.

questions.q: A customer asks for an extra feature mid-project. Which reply manages scope best?
choices: That is not possible, it is out of scope.
We can add it. It is about three days of work, which would move the release from 11 to 18 June. Shall we proceed, or ship it in the following release?
Sure, no problem, we will add it.
Please be advised that such requests cannot be entertained at this stage.
questions.explain: C isteği reddetmiyor, **bedelini görünür kılıyor** ve kararı müşteriye bırakıyor. A kapsamı sessizce şişirir (scope creep), B gerekçesiz kapıyı kapatır, D ise hem eski hem soğuk bir kalıp kullanır.

questions.q: Which requirement-gathering question is most useful?
choices: Do you want it to be fast?
You want a dashboard, right?
Could you walk me through how you do this today?
Should we use PostgreSQL or MySQL?
questions.explain: B açık uçludur ve mevcut süreci ortaya çıkarır; gerçek gereksinimler genellikle orada saklıdır. A ve C kapalı ve yönlendiricidir (müşteri 'evet' der, bilgi çıkmaz), D ise müşterinin karar vermesi gereken bir konu değildir.

questions.q: 'Dear Sir or Madam' is the safest greeting for an e-mail to a client whose name you already know.
questions.explain: Yanlış. Adı biliniyorsa **Dear Ms Kaya** / **Dear Mr Aydın** kullanılır; 'Dear Sir or Madam' mesafeli ve kişisizdir ve yalnızca muhatap bilinmiyorsa (genel başvuru, kurumsal yazışma) uygundur. O durumda kapanış *Yours faithfully* olur.

questions.q: Writing 'due to a number of unforeseen circumstances beyond our control' is a professional way to explain a delay.
questions.explain: Yanlış. Bu kalıp sorumluluğu dağıtır ve hiçbir bilgi vermez. Profesyonel biçim somut nedeni ve düzeltici eylemi verir: *We tested with a small dataset and did not see the problem; we have added a production-sized test to our checklist.*

questions.q: Which two-word English term describes the uncontrolled growth of agreed project scope?
accept: scope creep
questions.explain: **scope creep** = kapsam kayması. 'creep' sinsice ilerlemek demektir: tek tek küçük görünen istekler toplamda tarihi ve bütçeyi bozar. Panzehiri her isteği **change request** olarak kaydetmektir.

questions.q: Soften this request to a customer: 'Send me the production data today.' Begin with 'Could'.
accept: could you send me the production data today
could you please send me the production data today
could you send us the production data today
questions.explain: Emir kipi kılavuzda doğru, insana yönelik ricada serttir. **Could you (please)...?** en güvenli yumuşatmadır. Daha dolaylı: *Would you mind sending...?* / *It would be helpful if you could send...*

questions.q: Rewrite without the tired cliché: 'We apologize for any inconvenience this may have caused.' Write a concrete apology beginning with 'I am sorry'.
accept: i am sorry for the late notice
i am sorry for the delay and for the late notice
i am sorry that you had to find this out from your own customer
i am sorry for the disruption this causes
i am sorry for the change at short notice
questions.explain: Somut özür, neye üzüldüğünü söyler: *I am sorry for the late notice.* / *I am sorry for the disruption this causes.* Ardından düzeltici eylem gelirse özür inandırıcı olur: *...we have added that step to our checklist.*

questions.q: Translate into customer English: 'Bunu değişiklik talebi olarak kaydedip maliyetini çıkaralım.'
accept: let me note that as a change request so that we can cost it properly
let us note that as a change request so that we can cost it properly
let me record that as a change request so that we can cost it properly
let us record this as a change request and estimate the cost
questions.explain: Kalıp: **note / record something as a change request** + **so that we can cost it** (maliyetini çıkarmak). 'to cost' burada geçişli fiildir: bir işin maliyetini hesaplamak. Bu cümle reddetmeden kapsamı korur.

questions.q: Which sentence translates the technical cause into customer language correctly?
choices: The ORM produced an N+1 query pattern and the cache was not invalidated.
There were some technical issues on the backend side.
The system has a performance bug.
The report page sends one database request for each course, so it needs about 40 seconds to open with your 3,400 courses.
questions.explain: B hem **mekanizmayı** jargonsuz anlatıyor hem **müşterinin verisiyle** ölçülebilir etki veriyor. A müşteri için anlamsız, C ve D ise hiçbir bilgi taşımıyor ve güven kaybına yol açıyor.

questions.q: Write a customer e-mail in English (120-180 words) announcing that a data migration will take one extra week because 3 of 40 tables need manual work. Include subject line, the news in the first sentence, a jargon-free reason, a three-point plan, and a concrete apology.
rubric: Konu satırı haberi taşımalı (yeni tarih içermeli)
İlk cümlede yeni tarih ve gecikme süresi olmalı
Neden jargonsuz ve somut olmalı
Maddeli bir plan ve neyin değişmediği belirtilmeli
Somut özür ve düzeltici eylem içermeli
'I hope this email finds you well' ve 'unforeseen circumstances' klişelerini kullanmamalı
questions.explain: Örnek tam cevap: **Subject: Data migration: new go-live date 22 September (was 15 September)** *Dear Mr Demir, I am writing to let you know that the migration will go live on 22 September, one week later than planned. When we converted your database we found that 37 of the 40 tables transferred automatically, but three tables store dates in a format the new system reads differently. topics.title: Advanced Interview English: Behavioural Questions (STAR), Technical Interviews, Salary Negotiation
topics.summary: Davranışsal soruları STAR yöntemiyle yanıtlama, teknik mülakatta sesli düşünme ve bilmediğini doğru söyleme, maaş ve koşul görüşmesinin ölçülü ama doğrudan dili.
topics.notes:
## 1. Üç Tür Mülakat Sorusu

MI-1'de temel mülakat İngilizcesini gördük (kendini tanıtma, güçlü-zayıf yönler). Şimdi derine iniyoruz. Mülakat soruları üç kümeye ayrılır:

| Tür | Örnek | Beklenen cevap biçimi |
|---|---|---|
| **Behavioural** (geçmiş davranış) | *Tell me about a time when you disagreed with a teammate.* | **STAR** |
| **Technical** | *How would you find a memory leak in production?* | düşünerek, sesli akıl yürütme |
| **Situational / hypothetical** | *What would you do if the release broke on Friday evening?* | karar + gerekçe + ödünleşim |

Davranışsal soruların sihirli ifadesi şudur: **"Tell me about a time when..."**. Bunu duyduğunda genel konuşma değil, **tek bir somut olay** anlatman beklenir.

## 2. STAR Yöntemi

| Harf | Ne anlatılır | Süre | Kalıplar |
|---|---|---|---|
| **S** ituation | bağlam: proje, ekip, ne zaman | %15 | *I was working on... / At the time, our team was...* |
| **T** ask | senin sorumluluğun, hedef | %15 | *My task was to... / I was responsible for...* |
| **A** ction | **sen** ne yaptın, adım adım | %50 | *First I... / Then I... / I decided to... because...* |
| **R** esult | sonuç, tercihen sayıyla + ders | %20 | *As a result... / We reduced... by 40% / What I took away was...* |

**BAD (genel, "biz" dili, sonuç yok):**
> We always work as a team and communication is very important. When there is a problem we solve it together. I am a good team player and I like challenges.

**GOOD (tek olay, "ben" eylemleri, sayısal sonuç, ders):**
> **(S)** Last year I was the only backend developer on a three-person project that exported monthly reports for about 400 users. Two weeks before the deadline our export started timing out. **(T)** I was responsible for the export endpoint, and my task was to make it usable again without delaying the release. **(A)** First I measured where the time went and found that we made one database query per row — about 6,000 queries for a single report. I rewrote that part as a single query with a join, but the page was still slow, so I also moved the file generation into a background job and added a progress indicator. Before I changed the interface I checked with our designer, because I did not want to break the layout she had planned. **(R)** The export time fell from 48 seconds to 1.9 seconds, and we shipped on the original date. What I took away was that I should measure before I optimize — my first guess about the cause had been wrong.

> [!ipucu]
> STAR'da en sık yapılan hata Action bölümünü kısa, Situation bölümünü uzun anlatmaktır. Mülakatçı **senin ne yaptığını** dinlemek ister. "We" yerine "I" kullan — takım çalışmasını anlatırken bile senin katkın belirgin olmalı.

## 3. Sık Sorulan Davranışsal Sorular ve Cevap Açıları

| Soru | Ne ölçüyor | Cevapta olması gereken |
|---|---|---|
| *Tell me about a time you disagreed with a colleague.* | çatışma yönetimi | gerekçeyle itiraz, karşı tarafı dinleme, kararın nasıl alındığı |
| *Describe a mistake you made.* | sorumluluk alma | hatayı kabul, etkisini ölçme, kalıcı düzeltme (süreç değişikliği) |
| *Tell me about a time you had to learn something quickly.* | öğrenme becerisi | kaynak seçimi, ilk çalışan sonuç, süre |
| *Give me an example of working under pressure.* | önceliklendirme | neyi erteledin, neden |
| *Tell me about a time you received difficult feedback.* | olgunluk | ilk tepkini bastırma, eylem, sonuç |
| *Describe a project that failed.* | dürüstlük | neden başarısız oldu, ne öğrendin, tekrarını nasıl önledin |

Kaçınılacak cevaplar: *"I have never made a mistake."* (inandırıcı değil), *"My weakness is that I work too hard."* (klişe), başka birini suçlamak, soruyu genel bir felsefeye çevirmek.

## 4. Teknik Mülakatta Sesli Düşünmek

Teknik mülakatta tek doğru cevap nadiren vardır; **nasıl düşündüğünü** izlerler. Önce soruyu daralt, sonra yüksek sesle ilerle.

Açıklama isteme: *Before I start, may I ask a couple of questions about the requirements?* / *Should I assume the input fits in memory?* / *Are duplicates possible?*
Sesli düşünme: *Let me think out loud for a moment.* / *A naive approach would be ..., which is O(n squared). Let me see whether we can do better.* / *I will start with the simplest version that works and then optimize.*
Düzeltme: *Actually, that would fail if the list were empty — let me handle that case first.*
Bilmediğini söyleme (doğru biçimi): *I have not used that API, but I would expect it to work like ... . I would check the documentation before committing to that.*
Ödünleşim dili: *We could cache the result, but then we would need an invalidation strategy; given that the data changes once a day, I think the trade-off is worth it.*

> [!dikkat]
> "I don't know." cümlesini çıplak bırakma. Doğru biçim: **"I don't know that off the top of my head, but here is how I would find out."** Bilmemek kusur değil, yöntemsizlik kusurdur.

## 5. Maaş ve Koşul Görüşmesi

Maaş konuşması İngilizcede doğrudan ama ölçülü yapılır. Türkçedeki çekingenlik ("ne verirseniz") İngilizce görüşmede zayıflık olarak okunur.

| Durum | Kalıp |
|---|---|
| Erken sorulursa erteleme | *I would prefer to learn more about the role first. Could you share the budgeted range for this position?* |
| Aralık verme | *Based on what I have seen for similar roles in Ankara, I am looking for a gross monthly salary in the range of 65,000 to 75,000 TL.* |
| Gerekçelendirme | *That reflects my two years of backend experience and the on-call responsibility in this role.* |
| Karşı teklif | *Thank you for the offer. I am very interested, but the base is below what I had in mind. Would 72,000 be possible?* |
| Paketin tamamı | *If the base is fixed, could we look at the other elements — training budget, remote days or an earlier review?* |
| Süre isteme | *Could I have until Friday to consider the offer?* |
| Kabul | *I am happy to accept. Could you send the contract and confirm the start date?* |
| Nazik ret | *I have decided to accept another offer that is closer to my goals. Thank you for your time, and I hope we stay in touch.* |

Terimler: **gross / net** (brüt / net), **base salary** (taban ücret), **benefits** (yan haklar), **bonus**, **equity / stock options**, **notice period** (ihbar süresi), **probation period** (deneme süresi), **market rate** (piyasa düzeyi), **counter-offer** (karşı teklif), **non-negotiable** (pazarlığa kapalı), **compensation package** (ücret paketinin tamamı).

## 6. REAL TEXT — Interview Extract

```text
INTERVIEWER: Tell me about a time when you disagreed with a teammate about a
technical decision.

CANDIDATE: Sure. Last spring I was on a two-person team building an internal
tool for our department; we had about six weeks. My colleague wanted to store
the uploaded files in the database as binary columns, and I thought they should
go to object storage with only the metadata in the database.

My task was to design the storage layer, so the decision was mine to propose,
but I did not want to override him without understanding his reasoning. I asked
him to walk me through his concern, and it turned out that he was worried about
backups: with two systems, a restore could leave the database and the files out
of step.

That was a fair point, and I had not thought about it. So I did two things.
First I measured what we were actually dealing with: the average file was 4 MB
and we expected around 20,000 files, which is 80 GB - too much for our database
plan. Then I wrote a short comparison of the two options with a section on
backup consistency, and proposed storing a checksum and an upload timestamp so
that a mismatch after a restore could at least be detected. We took it to our
lead together, and she agreed with object storage plus the checksum.

As a result we shipped on time, and the restore check actually caught a
corrupted upload two months later. The thing I learned was that behind a
technical disagreement there is often a risk the other person can see and I
cannot - asking him to explain it first was what made the conversation useful.

INTERVIEWER: And if the two of you had not reached agreement?

CANDIDATE: Then I would have written both options down with the trade-offs and
asked our lead to decide, rather than letting it block the sprint. I would
rather have a decision I disagree with than an open question nobody owns.
```

Cevabın yapısı: S (bahar, iki kişilik ekip, altı hafta) - T (depolama katmanı benim sorumluluğum) - A (dinledim, ölçtüm, karşılaştırma yazdım, uzlaşma önerdim, lidere taşıdık) - R (zamanında teslim, checksum gerçek bir hatayı yakaladı, çıkarılan ders).

## 7. VOCABULARY

| English | Türkçe | Short definition |
|---|---|---|
| behavioural question | davranışsal soru | a question about what you actually did in the past |
| STAR method | STAR yöntemi | answering with Situation, Task, Action, Result |
| to walk someone through | adım adım anlatmak | to explain something in detail, step by step |
| to think out loud | sesli düşünmek | to say your reasoning while you work |
| off the top of my head | ezbere, hemen akla gelen | without checking, from memory |
| to take ownership | sahiplenmek, sorumluluğu almak | to accept responsibility for an outcome |
| to own up to (a mistake) | (hatayı) kabul etmek | to admit a fault openly |
| to override (a decision) | (kararı) geçersiz kılmak | to reject someone's decision with authority |
| to reach agreement | anlaşmaya varmak | to come to a shared decision |
| fair point | haklı nokta | a valid argument from the other side |
| out of step | uyumsuz, birbirini tutmayan | not matching or synchronized |
| takeaway / lesson learned | çıkarılan ders | what you concluded from the experience |
| compensation package | ücret ve haklar paketi | the whole of salary plus benefits |
| base salary | taban ücret | the fixed part of the pay |
| gross / net | brüt / net | before / after tax and deductions |
| benefits | yan haklar | non-salary elements such as insurance or meals |
| equity / stock options | hisse / hisse opsiyonu | a share of ownership offered as pay |
| market rate | piyasa düzeyi | the usual pay for that role and level |
| counter-offer | karşı teklif | a higher figure proposed in response |
| non-negotiable | pazarlığa kapalı | fixed and not open to discussion |
| notice period | ihbar süresi | how long before you can leave your current job |
| probation period | deneme süresi | an initial period with easier termination |
| to decline an offer | teklifi nazikçe reddetmek | to refuse politely |
| red flag | uyarı işareti | a sign that something may be wrong |
keyPoints: 'Tell me about a time when...' sorusu genel konuşma değil tek bir somut olay ister.
STAR dağılımı: Situation %15, Task %15, Action %50, Result %20. Action en uzun bölümdür.
Takım çalışmasını anlatırken bile 'I' kullan; mülakatçı senin katkını ölçer.
Result bölümünde sayı ver ve bir ders ekle: 'The export time fell from 48 s to 1.9 s. What I took away was...'
Teknik mülakatta önce soruyu daralt, sonra sesli düşün: 'May I ask a couple of questions about the requirements?'
'I don't know' çıplak bırakılmaz: 'I don't know that off the top of my head, but here is how I would find out.'
Maaşta aralık ver ve gerekçelendir: 'I am looking for a gross monthly salary in the range of X to Y, which reflects...'
Taban ücret sabitse paketin diğer unsurları görüşülür: eğitim bütçesi, uzaktan çalışma günleri, erken değerlendirme.
Hata sorusunda sorumluluk alınır ve kalıcı süreç düzeltmesi anlatılır; başkası suçlanmaz.
pitfalls: Davranışsal soruya genel felsefeyle cevap vermek: 'Communication is very important, I am a team player.'
Situation bölümünü uzatıp Action bölümünü iki cümleye sıkıştırmak.
Her cümlede 'we' demek ve kendi katkısını görünmez kılmak.
'My weakness is that I work too hard' ya da 'I have never made a mistake' gibi klişe ve inandırıcı olmayan cevaplar.
Maaş sorusuna 'whatever you think is appropriate' demek: İngilizce görüşmede hazırlıksızlık olarak okunur.
Teklifi hemen kabul ya da ret yerine süre istemeyi bilmemek: 'Could I have until Friday to consider it?'

flashcards.a: Situation (bağlam), Task (senin sorumluluğun), Action (ne yaptın - en uzun bölüm), Result (sonuç + ders).

flashcards.q: off the top of my head

haklı nokta - That was a fair point, and I had not thought about it. (Karşı tarafı kabul etmenin kısa yolu.)
sahiplenmek, sorumluluğu almak - I took ownership of the incident and wrote the postmortem.
