questions.q: In the interview extract, which part of the answer is the TASK?
choices: My task was to design the storage layer, so the decision was mine to propose.
We shipped on time and the restore check caught a corrupted upload.
I measured the average file size and wrote a comparison of the two options.
Last spring I was on a two-person team building an internal tool.
questions.explain: Task, **senin sorumluluğunu ve hedefini** tanımlar. A situation (bağlam), C action (eylemler), D result (sonuç). STAR'ın dört parçasını ayırt etmek sınavda da mülakatta da ilk adımdır.

questions.q: What makes the candidate's ACTION section strong?
choices: It lists the technologies used in the project.
It describes concrete steps the candidate personally took, including asking the colleague for his reasoning and measuring the data.
It explains that the team is always collaborative.
It blames the colleague for the disagreement.
questions.explain: Action bölümünün gücü **birinci tekil, somut ve sıralı eylemlerden** gelir: dinledi, ölçtü, karşılaştırma yazdı, uzlaşma önerdi, karar için lidere taşıdı. Teknoloji listesi ya da genel övgü bu bölümün yerini tutmaz.

questions.q: An interviewer asks a question you cannot answer. Which response is best?
choices: I don't know.
I have never needed that, it is not really important.
I don't know that off the top of my head, but I would start by checking the profiler output and then read the library's documentation on connection handling.
Could we skip this question?
questions.explain: C bilmediğini kabul ediyor ama **yöntemini** gösteriyor. Mülakatçı için bu, yanlış bir ezber cevaptan daha değerlidir. B savunmacı ve küçümseyici, A ve D ise konuşmayı kapatır.

questions.q: In a STAR answer, the Action section should be the longest part.
questions.explain: Doğru. Mülakatçı **senin ne yaptığını** ölçer, bu yüzden Action cevabın yaklaşık yarısını kaplar. Situation ve Task birlikte üçte biri geçmemeli, Result ise sayı ve çıkarılan ders içermelidir. Yaygın hata, bağlamı uzun uzun anlatıp (Situation) kendi katkısını iki cümleye sıkıştırmaktır.

questions.q: If asked about salary expectations, answering 'whatever you think is appropriate' is considered polite and professional in an English-language interview.
questions.explain: Yanlış. Bu cevap hazırlıksızlık ve kendi değerini bilmeme izlenimi verir. Profesyonel biçim ya aralık vermek (*in the range of X to Y*) ya da bilgi istemektir: *Could you share the budgeted range for this position?*

questions.q: What do the letters S, T, A, R stand for? (write the four words in order)
accept: situation task action result
questions.explain: **Situation, Task, Action, Result.** Bu sıra, dinleyiciyi bağlamdan sonuca taşır ve cevabın dağılmasını engeller. Birçok ekip buna bir 'L' (Learning) ekler: sonuçtan çıkarılan ders.

questions.q: Complete the technical-interview phrase for asking to clarify before coding: 'Before I start, may I ask a couple of questions about the ___?'
accept: requirements
requirement
problem
constraints
questions.explain: **requirements** (ya da *constraints*). Soruyu daraltmadan kod yazmaya başlamak, gerçek işte de mülakatta da hata kaynağıdır. Tipik daraltma soruları: *Can the input be empty? Are duplicates possible? Does it fit in memory?*

questions.q: Rewrite using 'I' instead of 'we', keeping the same fact: 'We rewrote the query and we reduced the export time.'
accept: i rewrote the query and reduced the export time
i rewrote the query and i reduced the export time
questions.explain: Mülakatta takımın işini anlatmak gerekli, ama **senin katkın** ayırt edilebilir olmalı: *I rewrote the query and reduced the export time from 48 seconds to 1.9 seconds.* Her cümlede 'we' demek katkıyı görünmez kılar.

questions.q: Translate into interview English: 'Teklifi düşünmek için cuma gününe kadar süre alabilir miyim?'
accept: could i have until friday to consider the offer
may i have until friday to consider the offer
could i have until friday to think about the offer
would it be possible to have until friday to consider the offer
questions.explain: Kalıp: **Could I have until <day> to consider the offer?** Süre istemek zayıflık değil, profesyonel normdur; teklifi aynı telefonda kabul etmek beklenmez. 'I want time' gibi doğrudan biçimler sert duyulur.

questions.q: Which counter-offer is phrased best?
choices: That salary is too low, I deserve more.
I have another offer that pays much better, so you should improve yours.
I accept, but I am not happy about the money.
Thank you for the offer. I am very interested in the role, but the base is below what I had in mind. Based on similar positions, would 72,000 gross be possible?
questions.explain: B dört şeyi birlikte yapıyor: teşekkür, **ilgiyi teyit** (*very interested*), gerekçe (*based on similar positions*) ve somut bir rakamla nazik soru (*would ... be possible?*). A ve C baskı kurar, D ise hem kabul eder hem zemin bırakmaz.

questions.q: Answer this behavioural question in English using the STAR method (8-12 sentences): 'Tell me about a time when you made a mistake that affected other people.'
rubric: Tek bir somut olay anlatmalı, genel konuşmamalı
Dört bölüm de ayırt edilebilir olmalı (S, T, A, R)
Action bölümü en uzun olmalı ve 'I' ile yazılmalı
Hatayı kabul etmeli, başkasını suçlamamalı
Result bölümünde ölçülebilir bir sonuç ve kalıcı bir süreç düzeltmesi olmalı
Bir ders cümlesiyle bitmeli (What I took away was...)
questions.explain: Örnek tam cevap: **(S) In my third-year project I maintained the script that imported weekly sensor data for four other students. (T) I was responsible for the import, and the others depended on its output for their own analyses. (A) One Friday I changed the date parsing to support a new file format and pushed it without running the existing test file, because the change looked trivial. The script silently shifted every timestamp by one month, and two of my teammates spent a day analysing wrong data before anyone noticed. When I realized what had happened, I told the group straight away rather than trying to fix it quietly, reverted the change, and re-imported the affected weeks. Then I added a test with three sample files and a check that refuses any import in which more than 5% of timestamps fall outside the expected week. (R) The re-import took two hours and no further data was lost; the guard has since blocked two bad files. What I took away was that a change looking trivial is exactly when I am most likely to skip the test, so the test now runs automatically instead of depending on my judgement.**

questions.q: Write a short salary negotiation exchange in English (4-6 lines) in which the recruiter offers a base below your expectation. Include a range with justification, one question about the rest of the package, and a request for time.
rubric: İlgiyi teyit eden bir teşekkür cümlesiyle başlamalı
Aralık vermeli ve brüt/net ayrımını belirtmeli
Gerekçe sunmalı (deneyim, sorumluluk, piyasa düzeyi)
Taban sabitse paketin diğer unsurlarını sormalı
Düşünmek için nazikçe süre istemeli
Agresif ya da özür dileyen bir ton kullanmamalı
questions.explain: Örnek tam cevap: **Thank you for the offer — I am genuinely interested in the role and in the team. Based on what I have seen for similar backend positions in Ankara, I was expecting a gross monthly salary in the range of 65,000 to 75,000 TL; the offer of 58,000 is below that. That range reflects my two years of production experience and the on-call rotation that comes with this role. If the base is fixed for this level, could we look at the rest of the package — for example a training budget, two remote days a week, or a salary review after six months? Either way, could I have until Friday to consider the offer properly? I will come back to you with a clear answer by then.**

topics.title: Working Internationally: Cross-cultural Communication, Remote Written Communication, Conferences and Community
topics.summary: Doğrudan ve dolaylı iletişim kültürleri arasında açık ama yumuşak yazma, eşzamansız uzaktan iletişimin kuralları, durum güncellemesi ve konferans bildiri özeti yazımı.
topics.notes:
## 1. Uluslararası Takımda İngilizce: Ortak Dil, Farklı Beklentiler

Uluslararası bir ekipte İngilizce konuşanların çoğu **ana dili İngilizce olmayan** kişilerdir. Bu, dili kolaylaştırır (kimse deyim yağmuru beklemez) ama **iletişim üslubunu** karmaşıklaştırır: aynı cümle farklı kültürlerde farklı okunur.

| Doğrudan (low-context) kültürler | Dolaylı (high-context) kültürler |
|---|---|
| Hollanda, Almanya, İskandinavya, İsrail | Japonya, Türkiye, Hindistan, Kore, çoğu Arap ülkesi |
| *This design will not work, because...* | *I wonder whether we should also consider another option.* |
| Eleştiri açık söylenir, kişisel değildir | Eleştiri yumuşatılır, bağlamdan anlaşılır |
| Sessizlik = onay değil, görüş yok | Sessizlik = çoğu zaman 'hayır' |

Pratik sonuçlar:
- Hollandalı bir meslektaşın *"I disagree, this is a bad idea"* dediğinde sana kızmamıştır; fikri reddetmiştir.
- Japon ya da Türk bir meslektaş *"That might be a little difficult"* dediğinde büyük olasılıkla **hayır** demiştir.
- Amerikan üslubunda *"Great work! A few small things..."* kalıbındaki 'few small things' aslında asıl mesajdır.

Güvenli yol: **açık ama yumuşak** yaz, ve anladığını **geri söyleyerek** doğrula.

| BAD | GOOD |
|---|---|
| Your plan is wrong. | I may be missing something, but I think the plan breaks when the file is empty. Could we check that together? |
| Maybe we could perhaps possibly consider thinking about it. | I would prefer option B, mainly because it needs no migration. What do you think? |
| Okay. (sessiz kalıp sonra yapmamak) | I can do it by Thursday, but not by Tuesday — Tuesday would mean dropping the tests. |

Anladığını doğrulama (**paraphrasing back**): *Just to make sure I understood: you want the export to include archived courses, but not deleted ones. Is that right?*

## 2. Uzaktan ve Eşzamansız (Async) Yazılı İletişim

Farklı saat dilimlerinde çalışan ekipte kural şudur: **yazılı olan olmuştur.** Konuşulan ve yazılmayan karar, yoktur.

| İlke | Uygulama |
|---|---|
| Bağlamı mesaja koy | Soruyu tek mesajda sor: *"Hi — quick question about the export: should archived courses be included? Context: ticket KRK-778, the spec does not say. My assumption is no."* |
| 'Hello' yazıp bekleme | *Hi, are you there?* tek başına bir saat kaybıdır. |
| Kararı belgeleyin | *Decision: we will include archived courses. Owner: Mert. Recorded in KRK-778.* |
| Engeli bekletme | *I am blocked and will work on KRK-812 instead until I hear back.* |
| Örtüşme saatlerini kullan | *Our overlap is 14:00-16:00 CET; I will keep synchronous topics for that window.* |
| Durum güncellemesi yaz | kısa, maddeli, tarihli |
| Sessizliği yanlış okuma | *No reply yet — I will assume no objection and proceed on Friday. Shout if that is wrong.* |

Kısaltmalar: **EOD** (end of day), **EOW** (end of week), **ETA** (estimated time of arrival/availability), **AFK** (away from keyboard), **OOO** (out of office), **PTO** (paid time off), **ASAP** (dikkatli kullan, baskı kurar), **FYI**, **TL;DR** (too long; didn't read — uzun mesajın başına özet).

> [!ipucu]
> Deyim ve yerel göndermelerden kaçın: *"let us touch base", "it is not rocket science", "we are not out of the woods yet", "to hit it out of the park"* (beyzbol) — ana dili İngilizce olmayan takım arkadaşların bunları anlamayabilir. **Inclusive, plain English** yaz: *let us meet briefly*, *this is simple*, *the problem is not solved yet*.

## 3. Konferans, Topluluk ve Açık Kaynak

**Call for papers (CFP)** bir konferansın bildiri çağrısıdır. Tipik gönderi parçaları: *title, abstract (150-250 words), session format (talk / lightning talk / workshop), target audience, takeaways, speaker bio*.

Biçimler: **keynote** (açılış konuşması), **talk** (25-40 dk), **lightning talk** (5 dk), **workshop**, **panel**, **poster session**, **BoF** (birds of a feather, serbest oturum). Kişiler: **speaker**, **attendee**, **organizer**, **chair** (oturum başkanı), **sponsor**.

Ağ kurma (networking) kalıpları: *What brings you to the conference?* / *What are you working on at the moment?* / *Could I ask what you use for X?* / *It was good to meet you — may I connect with you on LinkedIn?* / *I will send you that link tonight.*

Soru-cevap (Q&A) yönetimi: *That is a good question — I do not have data on that, but my guess would be ... .* / *Could you repeat the last part? I want to make sure I answer the right question.* / *Let us take that one after the session, so we stay on time.*

Açık kaynağa katkı dili:
- Issue açarken: *Thanks for this library. I may be doing something wrong, but ...* + sürüm, adımlar, beklenen/gözlenen.
- PR açarken: *This is my first contribution here, so please tell me if I should split it differently.*
- Maintainer'a saygı: *I understand you maintain this in your free time; no rush from my side.*
- Code of Conduct: topluluk davranış kuralları — her büyük projede vardır ve bağlayıcıdır.

CFP SUBMISSION - KRK DevDays 2026

Title
  What We Learned from 40 Slow Pages: Finding the Real Bottleneck

Session format
  Talk, 30 minutes, followed by 5 minutes of questions.

Abstract (212 words)
  Most performance work starts with a guess, and most guesses are wrong. Over
  eighteen months our team profiled 40 slow pages in a university course
  platform used by 12,000 students. In only 6 of those cases was the cause the
  one the team had assumed before measuring.

  This talk presents what the remaining 34 cases had in common. We show how a
  simple four-step routine - reproduce, measure, form one hypothesis, change one
  thing - replaced a culture of speculative optimization, and how we made the
  routine cheap enough that a student assistant can follow it. We will walk
  through three cases in detail: a page that made 3,400 database queries, a
  report that was slow only for users in one time zone, and an endpoint whose
  latency doubled after a library upgrade that touched none of our code.

  Attendees will leave with a printable checklist, a minimal profiling setup
  for Python and JavaScript applications, and a set of questions to ask before
  anyone is allowed to optimize anything. No prior profiling experience is
  assumed; the examples use open-source tools only.

Target audience
  Developers and students with at least one year of web development experience.

Speaker bio (60 words)
  Mert Aydin is a software engineer at KRK Software in Ankara, where he works on
  the platform team. He studied Computer Engineering at Kirikkale University and
  has been maintaining the open-source profiling helper "slowpoke" since 2024.
  He has spoken at two local meetups and this is his first conference talk.
